newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool indicator falls 1c to 592c/kg.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool indicator falls 1c to 592c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator eased 1.0 cent to 592 cents a kg clean on Wednesday at sales in Goulburn and Melbourne, Wool International (WI) said.
In merino fleece, the 19 micron indicator was 0.5 percent cheaper and the 20/21m 1.0 percent cheaper, while 22/23m was 1.0 percent dearer, it said.
The 24m indicator was slightly dearer, and 25m slightly cheaper.
Merino skirtings of 19 micron were 1.0 percent cheaper, and 20/21/22m generally unchanged.
In crossbreds, 26m was slightly cheaper, 27/28/29m slightly dearer, 30m up to 1.0 percent dearer and 31m unchanged.
In cardings, lambs of 19m and finer were 2.0 percent dearer while other lambs and locks and crutchings were unchanged.
Of the 25,157 bales offered, 7.9 percent was passed in.
WI said Japan and China were the principal buyers with support from Western Europe and most sectors of the trade.
Sales continue on Thursday in Goulburn, Melbourne and Fremantle with about 41,000 bales on offer.
